events.title: October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% from 3.6% and core PCE came in at 3.3%, above forecasts, cementing expectations of a Fed rate hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting.
The US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, up to 40% on China and 35% on Vietnam, sparing Mexico for now; stocks fell sharply and comments are due Jan 5.
events.who: USTR, China, Vietnam, EU, Japan, India

events.title: ING and Societe Generale are trying to sell up to $800M of AI data-center loans and HSBC reportedly sold about $300M at a discount, with New Mexico project loans in the mid-80s cents.
SpaceX shares fell toward $115, about 49% below their record high and below the $135 IPO price, on fears a $3.5T all-stock Tesla merger would dilute holders by roughly half.
Anthropic stock is down about 33% as investors weigh roughly $900B of AI spending commitments and an expected junk-range debt rating.
Cox Automotive forecast November new-vehicle sales of 1.20M, down 7.3% from a year ago on fewer selling days, with the annual pace steady at 15.8M and loan rates rising.
Bond investors expect Anthropic's planned debt to be rated BB, below investment grade, as it weighs borrowing on top of about $900B in commitments.
CoreWeave's 2031 bonds sold off, pushing their yield to about 17.9%, while its shares fell about 10% during the tech sell-off.
Nvidia led a tech sell-off as the rally from Jensen Huang's return faded, with Amazon and Alphabet down about 2% and Meta up 3%.
The chip index fell as much as 8% in the morning and the Nasdaq 100 briefly entered a bear market before both recovered to close down under 1%.
Jobless claims fell to about 189,000 and third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, keeping a December Fed hike in view.
SpaceX fell about 8% and Tesla nearly 6% as investors worried an all-stock merger would dilute SpaceX holders.
Anthropic shares slipped below their $83 IPO price in early trading, down about 5% near $82.78, erasing the gains from the Nov 19 debut.
Chip stocks fell back a day after their Nvidia-led surge, with the Nasdaq down about 1.8% and the S&P 500 down 1.3% in mid-session trading.
TSMC rose about 14% on Nov 23 to roughly $364, its best day since 2008, after losing about 20% the week before.
Tesla and SpaceX have named five directors to special committees handling merger talks, and Tesla's Dec 3 annual meeting agenda has no merger vote, the FT reported.
SpaceX's AI segment brought in about $7.56B in the third quarter, roughly 52% of revenue, mostly from leasing Colossus compute to Anthropic and Google.
The Conference Board's consumer confidence index jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, the highest since January 2025, as election uncertainty faded and gas prices fell.
Chowan County commissioners voted 3-2 for a one-year moratorium on new data centers, with residents citing strain on water and power during the state's drought.
The US is preparing new tariff increases on 16 economies under its Section 301 excess-capacity probe, with findings possible this week and the China truce expiring Jan 10.
events.who: China, EU, Mexico, Vietnam and 12 other economies

events.title: Neocloud stocks gave back Monday's rally, with CoreWeave down about 14% to $41.69, IREN down 15% and Nebius down 13%, while Nvidia fell about 8%.
Vistra's CEO said the midterms clarified data-center policy and forecast load growth of 4-6% a year in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM through 2030; its shares are down 14% since Nov 3.
AMD fell nearly 9% after a filing to resell 337 million shares and a new short report added to the chip sell-off.
Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his exit, and the shares jumped more than 30%.
US stocks rebounded sharply Monday with the Nasdaq up about 7% midmorning, recovering much of last week's correction after Huang's return.

nvidia.news: Nvidia led a Nov 25 tech sell-off as the rally from Jensen Huang's Nov 23 reinstatement faded, and the chip index fell as much as 8% intraday before closing down 0.7%. Analysts did not lift Big Tech capex forecasts after earnings (Nov 23).

labs.news: Anthropic closed at $82.79 on Nov 25, below its $83 IPO price, and bond investors expect its planned debt to be rated BB, below investment grade, against about $900B of spending commitments (Nov 25). No new OpenAI financing this week.

bigtech.news: Amazon and Alphabet fell about 2% and Microsoft over 1% on Nov 25 while Meta rose 3%; 2026 Big Tech capex is tracked near $730B. The 10-year Treasury is 4.91% and a December Fed hike is nearly priced in.

cloud.news: CoreWeave's 2031 bonds sold off to a yield near 17.9% and its shares fell about 10% on Nov 25, after a 14% drop on Nov 24; high-yield spreads are 3.72%, up 0.34 pt in 30 days. Data-center hubs face drought: Loudoun, Prince William and Dallas counties are 100% in drought.
cons: Record CDS spreads at Oracle and CoreWeave
cloud.weak: Bond markets now price a real chance that debt-funded neoclouds cannot refinance.

citizens.news: Core PCE inflation was 3.3% in October (Nov 25 report), energy CPI is up 21% y/y and household electricity prices 5.4%, with the saving rate at 4.1% and the 30-year mortgage at 7.21%. Grid demand in the lower 48 was up about 1.6% y/y in the latest EIA data (SRP Phoenix down 12%); Loudoun County, VA, is 100% in drought.

spacex.news: SpaceX fell about 8% on Nov 25 to near $116, below its $135 IPO price, on fears that an all-stock Tesla merger would dilute holders; a share unlock is due Dec 8. Colossus in Memphis keeps it tied to gas prices, with Henry Hub up $0.52 in 30 days to $3.30.

tesla.news: Tesla fell nearly 6% on Nov 25 as merger doubts grew, and an EU review of its driver-assist software slipped to Dec 15. Special committees on the SpaceX deal are not yet close to terms (Nov 24-25).

consumer.news: Consumer sentiment is 48, down 10% y/y, though the Conference Board index jumped to 103.3 in November (Nov 24). Adobe expects US online Black Friday sales of $12.9B, up 9%.

retail.news: Retail sales were up 6.8% y/y in October and e-commerce reached 17.9% of sales; Bain expects Black Friday-through-Cyber Monday sales to grow about 8.75%. New Section 301 tariff proposals (Nov 25) threaten import costs.

autos.news: Cox expects November new-vehicle sales down 7.3% y/y (Nov 25) and the annual sales rate is 16.1M; with the mortgage rate at 7.21%, auto credit stays expensive, and used-car prices are down 3.3% y/y.

fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% y/y and imports from Vietnam rose 61% y/y in September; proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to 20% on Chinese goods (Nov 25) add cost pressure for Shein and brands.

education.news: Student loans stand near $1.78T in the latest data, up 2.8% y/y. No notable new university or student-loan news this week.

banks.news: European banks are trying to sell up to $800M of AI data-center loans (Nov 25) and CoreWeave's bond rout signals losses on AI credit; BBB spreads widened 0.09 pt to 1.22% in 30 days.

fed.news: The fed funds rate is 3.88% inside a 3.75-4.00% target, but core PCE is 3.3%, well above 2%, jobless claims fell to about 189,000 and Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3% (Nov 25), so markets price a December 9 hike; unemployment is 4.1% and the mortgage rate 7.21%.

chips.news: AMD fell nearly 9% on Nov 24 on a 337M-share resale filing and a short report, and the chip index swung 8% intraday on Nov 25 before closing down 0.7%; TSMC ended at $342, down 2%.

power.news: Vistra forecast continued data-center load growth (Nov 24) and lower-48 grid demand is about 1.6% higher y/y; Henry Hub gas rose $0.52 in 30 days to $3.30.

healthco.news: Insurers fell on a proposed Medicare rule (Nov 23) while Eli Lilly agreed to buy LoQus23 for up to $725M; medical-care CPI is up 1.9% y/y.

industrials.news: No notable Boeing, Caterpillar or Lockheed news this week; new tariff proposals and AI capex doubts weigh on generator and equipment demand.

payments.news: Visa rose about 1.8% on Nov 25; card delinquency was 2.85% in the latest data, down from a year ago. A third-party breach disclosed Nov 19 did not touch card data.

trade.news: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs of 15-40% on 14 economies, including up to 20% on most Chinese goods (Nov 25); Canada and Mexico stay at 10% under the July action. Customs duties are down 17.5% y/y while imports from China rose 34% y/y in September.
